title: DOI Analysis Tutorial
subtitle: Step-by-step guide to analyzing research articles using a Digital Object Identifier (DOI)
about_body: This tutorial guides you step by step through analyzing a research article by DOI. A DOI (Digital Object Identifier) is a unique identifier system that lets us pull complete metadata for a scientific article automatically.

steps.title: Understand the DOI Format
steps.content: A DOI (Digital Object Identifier) is a unique identifier for a digital document. The standard format is: 10.xxxx/xxxxx
steps.tips: A DOI always starts with “10.” followed by a prefix and suffix separated by a slash (/).

steps.title: Find the Article's DOI
steps.content: The DOI is usually printed on the first page of a journal article, in the metadata section, or in the article URL.
steps.tips: Look for the label “DOI:” or “https://doi.org/” on the article page.

steps.title: Copy the DOI Correctly
steps.content: Copy the entire DOI string with no spaces or extra characters. Make sure there's no trailing period if the DOI appears at the end of a sentence.
steps.tips: Avoid copying “https://doi.org/” — copy just the DOI code (e.g. 10.1038/s41586-021-03616-x)

steps.title: Analyze the Research Profile
steps.content: Enter the DOI in Sciecola to analyze the research profile, citations, and links to SDGs.
steps.tips: The system automatically fetches complete metadata for a valid DOI.

errors.error: Whitespace at the start or end of the DOI
errors.solution: Make sure there's no space before or after the DOI
Remove the period if the DOI appears at the end of a sentence
Make sure you copied the full DOI including the suffix after the slash
